Along the Route 11 corridor you will find historic town centers full of older brick and stone homes, while the rest of the county is farms, river properties along the North Fork and mountain homes around Fort Valley and Basye. Wood heat is common here, and so are the problems that come with it: creosote, cracked liners and crowns weathered by valley winters. We sweep, inspect, repair and install throughout the county.

Amissville sits along Route 211 where Rappahannock County meets the Fauquier and Culpeper lines, a rural area of farms, pastures and country homes. Many properties rely on fireplaces or wood stoves through the cold months, and older masonry chimneys here often need crown, flashing or liner work to stay safe and dry. We sweep, inspect and repair, and we give you a clear estimate before any work begins.

As a small, local business, every job carries our name. That is why we take the time to do it right, from a routine sweep to a full stove and chimney installation.

As the county seat, Woodstock has a historic core full of older homes, while the farms and river properties around the Seven Bends of the North Fork add wood stoves and fireplaces that work hard all winter. Masonry chimneys here face harsh valley weather, and many older flues need liner work to safely vent a modern stove or insert. We sweep, inspect and repair, and we explain every finding clearly.
At the foot of the Blue Ridge near Thornton Gap, Sperryville homes and cabins rely on Rosas Chimney Services for chimney care.

At the western end of the W&OD Trail, Purcellville blends a historic town center with farms, wineries and newer neighborhoods. Older homes here often have masonry chimneys that need crown and liner work, while newer builds have prefabricated fireplaces that still need regular cleaning and inspection. We handle both, and we always leave your home clean.

Berryville and the surrounding Clarke County countryside are a regular stop for Rosas Chimney Services. We bring certified sweeps, inspections and repairs to homes in town and on the farms around it.

Older chimneys like these frequently have worn crowns, gaps in mortar and liners that need repair. We inspect to NFPA 211 standards, take photos of anything that needs attention and give you a straightforward estimate before any work begins.

An annual inspection, a sweep and a sturdy cap keep these chimneys working and keep animals and water out between visits.

Winchester's Old Town and its historic neighborhoods are full of 19th- and early 20th-century homes, many with multiple masonry flues that were built long before modern liners. Those chimneys often need a camera inspection and relining before they can safely vent a new stove, insert or furnace. In the newer subdivisions around the city, prefabricated fireplaces and metal chimneys are more common, and they need their own kind of attention. We work on all of it.
